changelog.content:
## Distribution

- Removed ARMv7 builds and release assets. Published binaries now target
  Linux and macOS on amd64 and arm64.

## Features

- Added the AI Gens package market and SDK-backed release downloads. Masters
  and Slaves can select the latest or an exact published version for signed
  managed updates; source releases dispatch publication to the public registry.
- Added unified fnOS gateway authentication and session handling for the
  embedded UI and gateway routes.

## Fixes

- Public TCP mappings now use a runtime-owned additive firewall chain. An
  ingress listener no longer enables the ordinary firewall's global default
  deny, so creating a mapping such as TCP 443 cannot silently block SSH or
  unrelated host services. Upgraded Slaves remove the legacy enforcing
  `AXON_SLAVE_FIREWALL_0` chain before reconciling mappings.
- Masters upgrading from the legacy `127.0.0.1:5004` Core endpoint now detect
  an authenticated pre-upgrade Core process still mapped from the replaced
  binary, request its supervised restart, and wait for it to return on
  `127.0.0.1:5204`. This also protects `core-ping` and `mesh-remove`, including
  fnOS packages whose separately installed root service points at the package
  binary.
- Role-specific Core installation refuses to activate `axon-core` and
  `axon-slave-core` in the same host network namespace. Core lifecycle dialogs
  now display the backend's concrete failure instead of replacing every error
  with a generic permission message.
- Fake TCP carrier forwarding now inserts its owned jump at the front of the
  host's effective `FORWARD` chain when xtables is available, so a later
  fnOS/Docker policy drop cannot discard already admitted carrier traffic.
- Fake TCP no longer marks a peer healthy from the unauthenticated outer
  SYN/SYN-ACK exchange. Route selection now waits for the WireGuard identity
  handshake, so a TCP-accepting black hole cannot starve a working Multi-Hub
  fallback path.
- Leaf-to-Hub routes and return routes from a secondary Hub now honor the
  Leaf's ordered Hub assignment in both directions. A flaky destination-Hub
  adjacency can no longer preempt the healthy primary backbone merely because
  the destination itself is a direct peer.
- Slave control retry delay resets after every established gRPC session, so a
  later topology-driven disconnect retries in three seconds instead of
  inheriting the maximum delay from failures before that session.
- Removing an already absent nftables firewall chain is now idempotent,
  including races where the last Axon table disappears during cleanup.
- Fleet plans are canonicalized by node, peer, and route identity. Transport
  validation compares membership and routes independently of vector order,
  preventing unchanged topologies from being rejected during hot switching.
- Reconciliation detects a committed peer set that conflicts with the
  canonical plan at the same immutable revision and atomically advances to a
  fresh revision before retrying. The same recovery handles a Core restart
  whose inactive persisted revision rejects the canonical payload, repairing
  fleets already affected by a disconnect/reconnect race.
- Unavailable public Hubs remain recovery anchors when no online replacement
  exists, preserving Fake TCP initiator/listener roles across restarts.
  Persisted Hub plans are now immutable within one revision, so a recovery
  membership change advances the revision before any online node is updated.
- SSH key-exchange deadlines now actively shut down the underlying socket.
  Cancelling a stalled russh handshake can no longer leave a detached
  connection alive until the five-minute inactivity timeout.
- Hub disconnect and reconnect events allocate distinct immutable revisions
  even when the preceding revision is still pending. Transport rollback stays
  active until the Master Core and every node acknowledge ABORT, and completed
  node rollback is now reported as `Rolled back` instead of `Rolling back`.
  Existing aborted transitions with a legacy pending Master row are repaired
  during database migration.
